title: human_config and halt_config, from Verify control.schema.yaml at 96ea36b6

human_config.description:
Required when the mechanism kind is `human` (all five flavors; a
`human-halt` control carries `halt_config` beside it). Names the
oversight pattern — one of the fourteen in
framework/schema/registries/human-patterns.yaml — and the settings
that differ from that pattern's defaults. A corpus control states
what its source text requires; a deployment fills in the rest
(roles, deadlines, escalation queues) when it writes the bundle.
Decision names come from framework/schema/registries/human-decisions.yaml.
Only human controls carry a pattern. A gate or evaluation that
involves a person stays a gate or evaluation, with no pattern; if a
person must review its result, that review is a second control, of
kind `human`, with its own id. Every control carries only its own
mechanism's config block, so a human control carries no
gate_config, guardrail_config, eval_config or sanitizer_config. The
pattern must run under the control's flavor; the mechanism-coverage
auditor checks this, that every human control has the block, that no
other control has it, and that no control carries another
mechanism's block. See specs/decisions/adr-018-human-patterns.md.

pattern.description: The oversight pattern (human-patterns.yaml) this control runs.

subject_kind.description:
What the person judges: an action the system would take, a
behaviour over time, a change to the system, the system itself
(halt and restart), an output, two records that may be one thing,
an appeal against a decision, a rule to be set aside, a
conversation or run to take over, or the evidence for an
attestation. Consoles choose how to present an event by it.

trigger.description: What raises the event. Monitors also give the metric and threshold.

routing.description: Who may decide. A reviewer must hold the roles and attestations listed (specs/platform/humans.md §10).

attestations.description: Qualifications a reviewer must hold, checked against the overseer registry (overseer-registry.schema.yaml).

required.description: Votes needed to settle the event.

of.description: N_OF_M only — the number of reviewers asked.

independence.description:
Who may not decide: whoever proposed the subject, whoever
built or loaded it, the first decider (appeals), and anyone
in the first decider's reporting line.

split_vote.description: What settles a TWO_PERSON or N_OF_M event when the votes disagree.

accountable_owner.description: The role accountable for this control's oversight. It answers oversight-quality signals.

sla_target.description: How long reviewers have before the timeout behaviour applies.

at_risk_at.description: Fraction of sla_target after which the event shows as at risk.

claim_ttl.description: How long a claim holds the event for one reviewer.

escalation_chain.description: Ordered queues an event moves through on ESCALATE. After an escalation, the next queue's roles decide.

minimum_review.description: Whether a decision under minimum_review_seconds is refused or recorded with a warning.

late_decision.description: Whether a decision after sla_target, on an event still open, is accepted (its verdict is breached) or refused.

ai_recommendation.description: The judge agent that reviews the event before a person does, if any.

proof_event.description: The AUD event that records each decision (specs/corpus/aud-taxonomy.yaml).

shadow.description: Record "would have raised" events without routing them to anyone.

strength.description: Per environment, whether the control prevents, warns or only records.

halt_config.description:
Required when the mechanism flavor is `human-halt`. A halt
capability is a registered, exercisable system-level intervention point
that brings the AI system to a halt in a safe state. It is not a
per-call guardrail or per-step workflow pause — it sits above the
runtime call layer and is exercised by oversight personnel.
Restarting is a decision under the control's human_config
(pattern `halt-restart`).

scope.description:
Scope of the halt: the full AI system, a specific service within
it, or a single capability/agent. Most regulatory halt
obligations are scope=system (one switch covers everything).

exerciser_personae.description:
Oversight roles authorized to exercise the halt — e.g.,
["safety-officer", "incident-commander"]. The implementation must
bind these roles to authenticated identities.

exercise_endpoint.description:
The registered intervention point through which oversight
personnel invoke the halt. Typically an HTTP endpoint
(e.g., "POST /api/halt") with strong auth; may be a CLI
command or a UI button — the spec is implementation-agnostic.

affected_calls.description:
What ceases when the halt is exercised. The strictest
(and most common) is `all-runtime-operations` — every
tool call, LLM call, and side effect denies until cleared.

target.description:
The service or capability a `service` or `capability` scope
stops. Deployment-applied; corpus controls leave it out.

emits_on_exercise.description:
The proof event recorded when the halt is exercised
(specs/corpus/aud-taxonomy.yaml: exerciser identity, scope,
reason, timestamp).

emits_on_lift.description:
The proof event recorded when the halt is lifted after the
restart decision (specs/corpus/aud-taxonomy.yaml).

safe_state_definition.description:
Optional plain-English description of what "safe state"
means for this system. Some regulations require the halt
to bring the system to a defined safe state, not merely
to stop.

duration.description: An ISO 8601 duration, e.g. PT30M or P30D.
